_README: Release attestations (GV-422) — read by tools/check-release-gates.mjs.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: some launch gates judge state that exists in NO repository.
The app-link association files are served from vehloshare.app but their contents
come from the Apple Developer / Google Play consoles (Team ID, signing SHA-256),
Sentry source maps live in a Sentry release that a build machine uploads, and the
Realtime "Allow public access to channels" switch is a checkbox in the Supabase
dashboard that no migration writes and no query reads (GV-490).
Nothing a CI job can grep proves any of them, so the only honest gate is a human
writing down what they checked, when, and under their own name — with an expiry,
because an attestation nobody has re-made in a month describes a state nobody has
looked at in a month.
HOW TO ATTEST (per entry):
1. Actually verify it. The 'note' field says what 'verified' has to mean; do not
lower the bar to the thing that is easy to check.
2. Set "state": "verified".
3. Set "verified_on" to today in YYYY-MM-DD (UTC).
4. Set "attested_by" to the person who ran the check (name or email) — an
unsigned attestation is not one, and the gate rejects it.
5. Commit it in the PR that made the state true, so the claim and the change are
reviewed together.
RULES THE GATE ENFORCES:
- state must be "verified"; anything else ("unverified", "expired", ...) is a
launch blocker: a warning locally, a hard failure under --strict.
- verified_on must be a YYYY-MM-DD date no more than 30 days old.
- attested_by must be non-empty; note must actually explain the item.
- Every entry below is seeded "unverified" on purpose, and a gate that starts
green would be a gate that never once told the truth. That includes
realtime_public_access_closed, which GV-490 added AFTER the switch was flipped
and checked in the dashboard on 2026-08-12: an agent may add the item, but only
the person who looked at the dashboard may sign for it, and only with a date
that is theirs. Re-check it, then attest it under your own name.
This file records CLAIMS, not secrets. Never paste a token, key, signing
fingerprint or Team ID into it — the repo is public.

app_link_secrets.note: Universal Links / App Links are live: https://vehloshare.app/.well-known/apple-app-site-association returns 200 as application/json with the real TEAMID.app.vehloshare appID and the /join/* + /auth/* paths, /.well-known/assetlinks.json returns 200 with the production signing SHA-256, _middleware does not intercept /.well-known/*, and a device test opens the app from a real invite link. See RENAME-VEHLOSHARE-RUNBOOK.md; the Team ID depends on the Apple enrollment tracked in GV-320.

sentry_source_maps.note: The mobile build being released has uploaded its source maps to the Sentry EU project (govehlo / react-native) under the matching release + dist, and a deliberately thrown error in that exact build symbolicates to a TypeScript file and line in the Sentry issue — not to a minified bundle offset. Checking that a sourcemap file was produced locally is NOT this attestation.

realtime_public_access_closed.note: Supabase Realtime is private-only in the PRODUCTION project, so the workspace topics cannot be read by anyone the RLS policies did not authorise (GVM-575, migrations 202/205/206; GV-490). All FOUR of these must hold, and each is a separate look: (1) Dashboard → Project Settings → Realtime → 'Allow public access to channels' is OFF in the production project (not staging, not the load-rehearsal throwaway); (2) a probe that joins presence-<any existing ledger id> WITHOUT private:true is REFUSED, with the platform's own reason 'PrivateOnly' — run `npm run probe:realtime-public-access` (SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, optionally SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN; it exits 0 only on a refusal); (3) a real member joining the SAME topic WITH private:true still reaches SUBSCRIBED, i.e. the switch closed the hole without taking presence and live sync down with it; (4) every mobile build in the field opens BOTH presence-<id> and ledger-changes-<id> with private:true — pre-launch, with no TestFlight or App Store build released, no other build exists, so this is trivially true and saying so IS the check; once builds are in the field it means the older public-channel builds are force-upgraded or gone. Reading this note, or reading that someone flipped the switch in a ticket, is NOT this attestation.
